subject: Feasibility: Acme Health on-prem + VPC deployment — governance & staffing questions
messages:

Cc: tim.omalley@acmehealth.com

Subject: Feasibility: Acme Health on-prem + VPC deployment (initial ask)

Hi Laura / Rafael,

Thanks for taking the time last week. Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for a private deployment option that must run inside our AWS GovCloud (VPC peering) and a restricted on-premise data center for a pilot. High level asks:

- PII-only data processing inside our VPC/on-prem; no tokens leave our network.
- KMS/HSM integration required (we use AWS KMS, and an on-prem SafeNet HSM for the data center).
- Patch windows must be coordinated; 24/7 availability during business-critical hours.
- Audit logs and retention for 7 years; SOC2 evidence may be requested during procurement.
- We expect ~35 qps during peak; model: 13B LLM quantized (we are flexible on model variant).

Attached is a short scope doc (acme_scope.pdf). Can you confirm feasibility and which Redwood teams we need to pull in for architecture, security sign-off, and on-prem ops? We're looking for an architecture feasibility review and a staffing estimate for a 90-day pilot.

Can we set a cross-functional call this week? Prefer Wed or Thu morning PST.

Thanks,

Anna Gupta
Head of AI Platform
Acme Health

Laura / team —

Thanks — quick technical readout from infra/serving side. Short answers first: yes, feasible with caveats. Details and open questions below.

Prelim capacity estimate (subject to workload profiling):
- Target: ~35 qps peak, 13B quantized model
- Ballpark: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to model serving (continuous batching) + 1 control host for routing and KV cache per deployment location (VPC and on-prem). We will need GPU isolation for customer data policies.

Open architectural questions (we need answers from Acme):
- KMS/HSM: Does the on-prem SafeNet expose PKCS#11 for signing/unwrap? We'll need either KMS integration or a local HSM plugin.
- Network: Will we have direct VPC peering to Redwood control plane for metrics/call-home? If not, we need an outbound-only proxy that can be audited.
- Storage: Where are model weights stored during runtime? If inside customer network, we need a secure model distribution mechanism (signed artifacts + attestation).
- Updates: What's the permitted patch/update cadence for models and runtime binaries on the on-prem hosts?

Nonstandard implementation items to note:
- HSM integration will require an engineering spike (2-3 weeks) and at least one security review.
- On-prem bootstrapping and offline install package (airgap) is additional effort — add 1 SRE and 1 infra engineer for 6 weeks for initial pilot.

I'm attaching a quick CSV with the capacity calc (prelim_capacity_estimate.csv). Will refine after we get answers to the open questions.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Folks — ops considerations and rough resourcing ask: 

Network and hosting:
- We need a dedicated VPC subnet and reserved IPs for the control plane endpoints. If peering is allowed, we recommend a single NAT gateway and strict security groups.
- For on-prem, the customer must provide a small bastion + an internal registry accessible to the hosts (signed images).

Monitoring / logging:
- Audit logs: ship to customer's secure S3 or on-prem log collector; retention policy configurable (7yr requested — will require lifecycle management and cost discussion).
- Tracing: sample at 0.1% by default; configurable for pilot.

SRE staffing & timeline:
- Pilot runbook + onboarding: 2 SRE engineers (0.5 FTE each) for 8 weeks to cover installation, runbook creation, and shadow on-call.
- Long-term support: recommend 1.0 FTE SRE + 0.5 infra for the first 3 months post-pilot, then reassess.

Compliance / legal asks:
- We'll need the customer's legal/itsec to sign an exception for outbound endpoints if any telemetry is enabled.
- KMS/HSM integration will need an SCO (security change order) and 3rd-party cryptography review.

Constraints & risks:
- We have a conflicting OS upgrade window on our internal Dedicated pool scheduled mid-August — suggests we should aim to avoid production cutover during that week.
- Airgapped installs have longer lead times (certs, packaging).

I can draft the ops runbook skeleton and share (ops_runbook_draft.md). Confirm if Acme can provide PKCS#11 details and a reachable bastion host.

- Dev
Dev Patel
